function.description: Bounded orientation from the remote memory graph (schema 3). Each page is authorized and measured independently; later pages are not prevalidated. A continuation whose bound service budget cannot fit returns a budget error; restart with a larger budget or narrow the query. Task state and candidates are unverified unless claim_status says verified. Remote failures are reported, never replaced with local results.
function.name: memory_orient

budget_bytes.description: Complete successful MCP response frame bytes, including JSON-RPC framing and newline, never exceed this budget. If too small for a compact budget error, that error exceeds the budget but is at most 512 bytes including newline. For continuation keep the effective budget unchanged; restarting the MCP server invalidates continuations. Request IDs are limited to 256 JSON-encoded bytes; larger IDs are rejected before execution with JSON-RPC invalid request and id null, so cannot be correlated.

function.description: Bounded passage of one cited stored source. Each page is authorized and measured independently; later pages are not prevalidated. Each service read revalidates and rereads the complete source. If a bound continuation cannot fit, restart with a larger budget or resume at the last passage end_byte and narrow the byte range with end_byte. Default publication mode is ID-only; working mode requires project_id and task_id and returns only sources cited by this client's own task candidates. Passage offsets are exact stored-artifact UTF-8 bytes; source evidence is never a verified claim. To continue, omit start_byte and keep other parameters unchanged.
function.name: memory_fetch

function.description: Submit a task-local candidate claim. The server derives origin; candidates are never verified by submission. Writes require a server-advertised revision bound and enough budget for the full revision receipt; otherwise no write is attempted. If the receipt is lost, the error is unknown_outcome: the write may have committed, so reread working state before retrying.
